newsitem.title: UK: POLL - Sterling keeps to strong side of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Sterling keeps to strong side of forecasts.

text.p: Sterling's spectacular rise in recent months has pushed its value against the dollar and the mark well above economists' expectations, according to a review of forecasts contained in year-old Reuters surveys.
The average of 29 predictions made last July for the pound against the dollar on June 30 was 1.4955, with the highest forecast, from Standard Chartered, at 1.63 dollars.
The forecasts were short of the actual rate on June 30 of 1.6650.
The experts were also caught out by the rise of sterling against the mark. The mean of 28 forecasts made 12 months ago was 2.2791 marks, with the highest prediction at 2.52.
In fact, sterling traded at 2.9035 marks on June 30, shortly before it made another surge to six-year highs around 3.0025 marks.

The pound has recently been buoyed by the new Labour government's first budget which did little do dampen consumer demand. It also benefited from four interest rate increases since last October, the most recent being a quarter-point rise last Thursday to 6.75 percent.
Five out of 29 forecasters in last July's Reuters survey made a successful prediction of the 6.50 percent base rate which prevailed on June 30.
They were Deutche Morgan Grenfell, Lombard Street Research, NatWest Markets, Stone and McCarthy Research and one unattributable forecaster.
